CT 3D:
**TECHNIQUE:**

Volumetric CT acquisition through [specified region] was performed. Multiplanar reformats and 3D volume-rendered images were generated.

**FINDINGS:**

Bone/soft tissue/vessels: [Describe any fractures, lesions, masses, vascular anomalies].

3D morphology: [Describe spatial relationships, prosthetics, surgical planning].

No additional abnormalities noted.

**IMPRESSION:**

3D reconstructions show [summary, e.g., "complex displaced mandible fracture involving the condyle"].

Recommend [surgical consultation, follow-up imaging].
CT Abdomen & Pelvis:
**TECHNIQUE:**

Axial CT of the abdomen and pelvis was performed with [oral/IV/both] contrast. Images reconstructed with multisequence.

**FINDINGS:**

Liver, spleen, pancreas, adrenals, kidneys: Normal size, shape & enhancement; no masses or ductal dilatation.

Bowel & Appendix: Normal caliber and wall thickness; no inflammatory changes or obstruction.

Vascular structures: Aorta, IVC, portal, mesenteric vessels unremarkable.

Lymph nodes/Retroperitoneum: No lymphadenopathy or free fluid.

Pelvis/Bladder/Reproductive organs: Normal appearance.

Bones/Soft tissues: No fractures or destructive lesions.

Lung bases: Clear; no effusions.

**IMPRESSION:**
No acute abnormality detected. [Add incidental noteworthy findings or recommendations as needed].
CT Abdomen & Pelvis Lifesaver:
**TECHNIQUE:**

Multiphase CT (non-contrast, arterial, portal venous ± delayed). IV contrast administered as per protocol.

**FINDINGS:**

Arterial phase: Evaluate for active extravasation or vascular injuries.

Parenchymal organs: Assess for lacerations, hematomas, infarcts; grade if present.

Bowel/transecting injuries: Evaluate wall thickness, free air/fluid.

Urothelial/excretory phase: Check for urinary leaks, collection in trauma.

**IMPRESSION:**

[E.g., "Grade III splenic laceration without active bleeding. No other visceral injury."]

Recommend trauma team review and follow-up imaging as per protocol.
CT Abdomen & Pelvis Triphasic:
**TECHNIQUE:**

Unenhanced series followed by arterial (~25–35 sec) and portal venous (~60–70 sec) phases, with optional delayed imaging.

**FINDINGS:**

• Arterial phase: Evaluate hypervascular lesions.

Portal venous: Assess overall organ enhancement, venous structures.

Delayed/excretory: Evaluate lesion washout, urinary tract.

**IMPRESSION:**

Example: "Segment IV liver lesion shows arterial hyperenhancement and washout in delayed phase suggestive of HCC."

Recommend MRI correlation or follow-up per clinical context.

**TECHNIQUE:**

**FINDINGS:**

**IMPRESSION:**

E.g., "Mild AAA of 3.5 cm; no dissection or stenosis."
